# Record 20260801-102353-79f398e

- **Record ID**: 20260801-102353-79f398e
- **Claim**: #4 -> #9 (design-input, not a spec line) -- small-signal output resistance and compliance boundary of six candidate charge-pump mirror stacks (simple / self-biased cascode / wide-swing cascode, both polarities) across the full PVT grid, sufficient to pick the stack and confirm compliance covers the VCO control range.
- **Netlist provenance**: schematic (`sim/devchar-cp/testbench/tb_cp_mirror.spice`) — **taken against a dirty working tree** at commit `79f398e9e9d3c4585c4cb74a77d5ec0b2fdaa65d`; not citable as a clean-tree result, netlist SHA-256 `81f14b746580a88f5346a35eb504c496ec1042ce6d06cd0c52dfac7d554347ba`
- **Environment provenance**:
  - PDK: volare `gf180mcuD`, open_pdks `c6d73a35f524070e85faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b` (/home/ubuntu/.volare/gf180mcuD, found via search_root:~/.volare)
  - Models: `libs.tech/ngspice/sm141064.ngspice`; `design.ngspice` included first
  - Simulator: ngspice-42 : Circuit level simulation program. Harness: sim/harness 0.1.0, python 3.12.3
  - Repo commit: `79f398e9e9d3c4585c4cb74a77d5ec0b2fdaa65d` (DIRTY tree)
  - Host: Linux-7.0.0-1009-aws-x86_64-with-glibc2.39 (ip-172-31-74-176)
- **Corner matrix run**:
  - Process (bundle -> `.lib` sections): `typical` -> typical res_typical moscap_typical mimcap_typical; `ff` -> ff res_typical moscap_typical mimcap_typical; `ss` -> ss res_typical moscap_typical mimcap_typical; `fs` -> fs res_typical moscap_typical mimcap_typical; `sf` -> sf res_typical moscap_typical mimcap_typical
  - Temperature: -40 °C, 27 °C, 125 °C
  - Supply: 2.97 V, 3.30 V, 3.63 V
  - 45 point full-factorial grid (process x temperature x supply), 45 completed
  - Full PVT matrix per CLAUDE.md / sim/README.md (-40/27/125 °C, ±10% supply, the five MOS process bundles).
- **Methodology / criteria / limitations**:
  - Measurement topology: each stack's output drain is tied through its own 0 V ammeter to a single swept node `sw`, shared by all six stacks; one DC sweep of `sw` from 0 to Vdd in 10 mV steps traces the complete output I-V of every stack in one analysis -- through the saturation knee and into triode, not just the flat region. A second `op` analysis records each polarity's reference-device operating point (vth / vdsat / gm / gds), because the compliance numbers are only interpretable next to the inversion level they were taken at.
  - ro(V) = |dVout/dIout| is the same +/-10 mV central difference on the 10 mV sweep grid the pre-migration extraction used, re-expressed as a pair of `.measure dc find ... at=` reads and a `param=` quotient; the P-polarity stacks carry an explicit leading minus because their output current falls as Vout rises. ro is reported at 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 x Vdd, as before.
  - Compliance is reported as a *knee ladder* rather than as the pre-migration record's single crossing voltage: chd0v20 / chd0v40 / chd0v60 / chd0v80 are Iout normalised to the stack's own mid-rail current, read at 0.20 / 0.40 / 0.60 / 0.80 V of headroom from the rail the stack works against (ground for the N sinks, Vdd for the P sources). The pre-migration `vcomp_i1pct` / `vcomp_i5pct` are the inverse function of this ladder -- the headroom at which the ratio reaches 0.99 / 0.95 -- and are read off it by interpolation. The change of form is forced, not preferred: ngspice's `.measure ... when <var>=<value>` cannot take a value derived from another measurement (`when i(vam_ns)='0.99*imid_ns'` fails at netlist-parse time with 'Undefined parameter'), so a threshold defined relative to a measured mid-rail current is not expressible as a manifest measurement. The ladder carries strictly more information than the two scalars it replaces.
  - `abstol=1e-16 reltol=1e-7 vntol=1e-9 gmin=1e-15` (the pre-migration deck's `.option` card, verbatim): the output-resistance extraction differences currents of order 10 pA over a 10 mV step, which the default abstol=1e-12 would otherwise dominate. Do not trust any ro above ~10 MOhm without this.
  - Sizing: NMOS W=5um, PMOS W=15um, L=1um (deliberately long-channel analog geometry, not the digital minimum-length devices in devchar-delay); cascode bias diode at W/4; Iref=20uA, chosen so both polarities sit in moderate inversion (Vdsat ~ 0.2 V) at Iref -- the regime a charge pump actually uses.
  - Statistical switches: sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0 (nominal device skew, no Monte Carlo). CP mismatch is a separate campaign (#15, mc-cp-mismatch), not this record.
  - LIMITATION -- one pre-migration column family and one artifact are NOT reproduced here. `vcomp_ro50` / `headroom_ro50` (the output voltage at which ro falls to 50% of its mid-rail value) requires walking the swept curve for a threshold crossing of a *derived* quantity, and `cp_curves.csv` is the decimated curve itself; the harness records scalar per-point measurements, so neither is expressible in a manifest today. Both remain committed, for this same deck and grid, under the superseded record 20260731-041340-833292f.
  - Agreement with the record this one supersedes (20260731-041340-833292f, same deck, same 45-point grid, run through the sim/lib/simenv.sh shim on ngspice-46/macOS rather than this harness on ngspice-42/Linux): over all 270 stack-corner rows of that record's cp_summary.csv the directly measured currents agree closely -- iout_mid and gain to <= 0.013 %, isat to <= 0.11 % -- as do the reference-device vth/vdsat. `ro` is the one column with percent-level differences (median 0.04-0.21 % by decade, p90 <= 1.4 %, worst 9.8 % on a 4e7 ohm p_casc point), and that is arithmetic, not physics: ro is a 20 mV difference quotient whose denominator is a sub-nanoamp current step, so it amplifies any current disagreement by ~5 orders of magnitude. Converted back to the physical quantity, the WORST ro disagreement in the whole grid corresponds to a 4.8e-11 A difference in a 2e-5 A current -- 2.4 ppm, i.e. solver-level. The two extractions also differ slightly by construction: the pre-migration awk took a central difference between adjacent 10 mV sweep samples at the grid point NEAREST 0.3/0.5/0.7 x Vdd, while `find i(...) at='0.3*vdd_val-0.010'` interpolates at exactly +/-10 mV about the target, which is off-grid whenever 0.3 x Vdd is not a multiple of 10 mV. The superseded record's own warning stands for both: do not trust an ro above ~10 Mohm as more than an order of magnitude. No conclusion of that record is changed -- the stack ranking by ro decade is identical.
- **Statistical convention**: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim)
